results.title: China and India in a standoff at multiple locations along Arunachal border since July, India hosted Xi Jinping from Sep 11-13 for the BRICS
results.description:
China and India in a standoff at multiple locations along Arunachal border since July, India hosted Xi Jinping from Sep 11-13 for the BRICS summit. 
“In the past few-days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues,” ITBP D-G Shatrujeet Kapur said on Thursday.
This is the first official confirmation of the scale of the continuing tensions on the north-eastern border since July this year.
Government sources told The Hindu that since late July, India and China have been engaged in a stand-off at Asaphila near Taksing in Arunachal Pradesh. The Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is said to have pitched tents at an elevation, within 6-7 kilometres of India’s perception of the Line of Actual Control (LAC) near Maja company operating base in Taksing circle of Upper Subansiri district, sources said. results.title: 🇮🇳🇨🇳 India and China are still facing off in Arunachal Pradesh India has officially confirmed that its troops are still involved in face-off
results.description:
🇮🇳🇨🇳 India and China are still facing off in Arunachal Pradesh

India has officially confirmed that its troops are still involved in face-offs with the Chinese military at several points along the Arunachal Pradesh border.

One of the main flashpoints is near Taksing in Upper Subansiri, where tensions have continued since July. Indian reports previously claimed that Chinese troops had set up tents several kilometres inside territory claimed by India.

And this never really stopped during the recent India-China rapprochement.

Xi Jinping visited India for the BRICS summit, officials held more border talks and both sides talked about improving relations.

Meanwhile, their troops were still blocking each other in Arunachal Pradesh.
